text:
Shirudo adds a Linux shield. It doesn't replace your patch.

WHAT CHANGED
OpenAI and Cisco announced Shirudo on Nov. 23: an open-source runtime for temporary protections on running Linux systems.

WHAT IT DOES
It uses eBPF, small programs attached at specific operating-system points, to target vulnerable behavior. Operators can evaluate a shield's impact before enforcing it. Security teams control deployment.

BUILDER VALUE
A blocked test is not the whole job. Normal requests still need to work, and the permanent patch still needs to ship. This is infrastructure work, not a browser extension for everyone.

TRY THIS
Open the official getting-started browser lab at https://labs.isovalent.com/#/lab/shirudo-getting-started this week. Follow the exercise and note what its verification proves. Don't start on production. For a deeper test, the VM quickstart walks through signing, loading, checking and unloading a protection.

THE SIGNAL
AI is moving into operational workflows. The human layer defines what safe and useful mean.

Source: OpenAI, Nov. 23: https://openai.com/index/introducing-shirudo/

Save this before your next AI infrastructure experiment.
